questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?

options.text: Ride with your headlight off.
Wear bright clothing.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Do not use turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible. Also use your headlight at all times and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if the clothing is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Choose sturdy material that fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What type of pants should a motorcycle rider wear for protection?

options.text: Pants made of soft material.
Pants made of heavy material.
Pants that fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Short pants that expose some of the legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or other sturdy material that cover your entire legs. The pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use that lane.
It would be hard to see traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. The vehicle could also block your escape route if another hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: Tire wear and tread.
How much cushion your seat has.
How shiny your paint is.
The wind direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire wear and tread.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What does having enough space between your motorcycle and other vehicles provide?

options.text: Time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement to one area of the lane.
Allows you to rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to drive faster than traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright clothing when riding. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so be visible at all times.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that lets you draft behind other vehicles.
The one that lets other drivers see you.
The one that puts you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that lets other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. Avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and surface hazards. Keep your space cushion large, discourage other drivers from sharing your lane, and give yourself an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What should your helmet do to protect you best?

options.text: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
Look sturdy.
Be inexpensive.
Be your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders watch for when passing parked cars?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space.
Cars pulling away from the curb or parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling away from the curb or parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Use caution when passing parked cars. Vehicles may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces suddenly.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, motorcycles can usually ride safely on this center strip.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always ride within a foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice you are braking.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Look only in your mirrors.
Use only your peripheral vision.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before you change lanes.

questions.question: Unlike food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes of drinking and affects you right away.
Alcohol never leaves your body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol quickly once it is in your system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes of drinking and affects you right away.
questions.explanation: Since it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour at a steady rate.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may speed until the pass is complete.
You may ignore "No passing" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must complete the pass at the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass at the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Complete passes at the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol's effects from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol's effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes varies, so it is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light when needed.

questions.question: If you think stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When stopping takes longer, give yourself more space between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you time to stop safely.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible. Keep the motorcycle straight and upright. Rise slightly off the seat before impact so your legs can help absorb the shock.

questions.question: What is an important reason to wear a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear when riding.
It provides protection in a crash.
It should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. It protects your skin in a crash. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: How can an applicant avoid taking the motorcycle skills test?

options.text: By completing an approved rider training course.
By scoring 95 percent or higher on the written test.
By having no moving violations on their driving record.
By applying in certain counties.

questions.correctAnswerText: By completing an approved rider training course.
questions.explanation: You can skip the skills test if you complete an approved rider training course that includes a similar skills test.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What makes riding at night safer?

options.text: It is not recommended.
Wearing reflective clothing.
Other drivers cannot see your turn signals at night anyway.
It should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Scan the road ahead and watch for potential dangers.
Focus on your controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are minimal.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the road ahead and watch for potential dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead to see potential hazards early. This helps you react before encountering them.

questions.question: What type of helmet gives the best protection?

options.text: One that fits snugly.
One that is well-worn and broken in.
One that is pretty loose.
One without a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
